runs.description: the air over the sea keeps its initial heat and moisture (no fluxes from the ocean)
uniform soil moisture everywhere (no wet or dry regions)
no mountains (no blocking, no orographic rain)
no daytime heating and no nocturnal cooling over land

limitations: a single coupled boundary layer with prescribed, moving Gaussian pressure systems: no dynamics of the pressure field, no jet stream or upper-level waves
the ensemble perturbs positions, speeds, deepening, genesis and the initial temperature; its errors grow roughly linearly, not chaotically
clouds, precipitation and severe convection are rule-of-thumb diagnostics every few hours; precipitation between diagnoses continues at the diagnosed rate
the land mask is real (global-land-mask), the terrain, sea-surface temperatures, soil moisture and the weather situation are synthetic
verification is against a member of the same model world, so it measures the predictability of this model, not the skill of a real forecast
floods are a runoff index (72-hour runoff from saturated soil and slopes), not a river routing; storm surge comes from the tropical-cyclone kernel

clouds.note: A frontal zone from 1 K per 100 km: the 210 km grid smooths the fronts.

ensemble.note: Ten members and a hidden truth member, all drawn from the same error distribution.

grid.note: The North Atlantic sector from the US Plains to central Europe and from the Caribbean to Iceland, in the local azimuthal-equidistant frame of 40 N, 45 W; 210 km cells.

gusts.note: The 10 m wind is the wind of the coupled 1.5 km layer slowed by surface friction (0.6 over land, 0.8 over the sea; mountains reduce it further), plus the hurricane vortex. Gusts: 10 m wind x 1.45, plus 8 m/s of downdraft under thunderstorms.

hurricanes.note: Tropical cyclones come only from the seeds (spontaneous genesis is off). On the 210 km grid their wind is a modified Rankine vortex (tropical-storm winds reach a few hundred km), with a rain shield and a coastal surge of at least a cell's width.

precipitation.note: Convective and frontal rain draws on the moisture of a 3 km deep layer down to 40 % relative humidity. Large hail reaches the ground in full where the freezing level lies below 3 km and not above 4.5 km: the column keeps a constant 6.5 K/km environment, so its tropical freezing level (about 4.4 km) sits lower than the observed 4.8-5 km.

sensitivity.note: The unperturbed control is rerun with one coupling switched off: what each link contributes to the forecast.

surface.land_mask_source: global-land-mask 1.0.0 (MIT; GLOBE 1 km elevation, NOAA), majority of 3 x 3 points per cell by tools/make_land_mask.py
surface.note: Sea-surface temperatures and land climate are rounded early-September values by latitude with the main currents as anomalies; soil moisture is a rough pattern.

terrain.note: Idealised Gaussian ranges at roughly the right places and heights (hand-entered), not a digital elevation model.

synoptic.note: A synthetic early-September situation, not a reconstruction: the subtropical high, the Icelandic low, a low over the Great Lakes that deepens over the Atlantic and reaches Europe, a lee cyclone forming within hours over the Central Plains at midday of the first day (severe thunderstorms in the moist, warm return flow from the Gulf), a cold high over Canada, a high over Europe, and new cyclones off the US East Coast every 2.5 days.

synoptic_weather.note: The ascent of the warm conveyor belt ahead of lows (strongest to the east-northeast) and the subsidence of highs, which the single layer cannot make itself: layered cloud and rain. Half of the upslope wind rises over the terrain (orographic cloud and rain on the windward slopes).

warnings.note: Levels yellow, orange, red; a level is issued where at least min_probability of the members exceed its threshold (tornadoes: tornado_min_probability; red needs red_min_probability). Gusts 18/25/33 m/s are about 65/90/120 km/h; thunderstorms: yellow any, orange hail of 3 cm, red hail of 5 cm. Floods: 40/80/150 mm of runoff in 72 hours (saturation excess from wet soils and slopes, a flood index rather than river levels).

static.land_mask_source: global-land-mask 1.0.0 (MIT; GLOBE 1 km elevation, NOAA), majority of 3 x 3 points per cell by tools/make_land_mask.py

verification.note: verified against a hidden member drawn like the others (the truth of the model world)
